content: Hello! how can I help today?
What’s the tax advantage of inheriting property instead of gifting it during life?

Assets transferred at death receive a **step-up in basis** under §1014. The basis resets to fair market value as of the decedent’s date of death.

This can eliminate capital gains built up over decades.
How do I prove the stepped-up value?
Obtain a **qualified appraisal** near the date of death. This establishes your new basis and prevents IRS challenges if you later sell the property.
Should I avoid gifting appreciated stock then?
Correct. If you gift appreciated assets during life, the recipient assumes your **carryover basis**. It’s usually more tax-efficient to pass assets at death, when possible.
For spouses in community property states, both halves get a step-up. In common law states, only the decedent’s half does. It’s critical to understand title and domicile rules.
